Q: Why does C#'s XmlWriter change a \n to a \r\n inside a text element? A:

Why does this code output true? I told the StringWriter to use \n newlines

This is expected behavior, given the code provided.

The StringWriter.NewLine property only applies to the StringWriter.WriteLine() method, which is not being used in this code.

You are not setting the XmlWriterSettings.NewLineChars and XmlWriterSettings.NewLineHandling properties, so their defaults of Replace and "\r\n" are being used, respectively. So, when you try to write a '\n' character using XmlWriter.WriteString(), it gets replaced with "\r\n", which is then written to the StringWriter.

Per Microsoft's documentation:

XmlWriterSettings.NewLineChars Property

The default is \r\n (carriage return, new line) for non-Unix platforms, and \n (new line) for Unix platforms.

XmlWriterSettings.NewLineHandling Property

The default is Replace.

...

The Replace setting tells the XmlWriter to replace new line characters with the character(s) specificed in the NewLineChars property. This setting also replaces new lines in attributes with character entities to preserve the characters. It is also the default value.

...

The following tables show the output of the WriteString method when supplied with the input value depending on the NewLineHandling property setting. The tables show the output when writing text content and also when writing an attribute value.

Text Node Value:

NewLineHandling \r\n \n \r \t
Entitize &#D;\n \n &#D; \t
Replace \r\n \r\n \r\n \t
None \r\n \n \r \t

Attribute Value:

NewLineHandling \r\n \n \r \t
Entitize &#D;&#A; &#A; &#D;
Replace &#D;&#A; &#A; &#D;
None \r\n \n \r \t

So, if you don't want the '\n' character to be changed, then set XmlWriterSettings.NewLineHandling to None, eg:

var settings = new XmlWriterSettings()
{
    NewLineHandling = NewLineHandling.None, // <-- add this
    OmitXmlDeclaration = true,
};

Q: No usable version of libssl was found Aborted (core dumped) (Powershell on ubuntu 21.04) A:

Please check my solution for Ubuntu 22.04+ and libssl1.1. Ubuntu 22.04+ only comes with OpenSSL 3.0 (libssl3) by default, and libssl1.1 has been deprecated from the official repositories. A possible workaround is to download an older package from the archive and install it manually via dpkg.

wget http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/o/openssl/libssl1.1_1.1.1f-1ubuntu2_amd64.deb

sudo dpkg -i libssl1.1_1.1.1f-1ubuntu2_amd64.deb

rm libssl1.1_1.1.1f-1ubuntu2_amd64.deb

The outcome:
...
Unpacking libssl1.1:amd64 (1.1.1f-1ubuntu2) ...

Setting up libssl1.1:amd64 (1.1.1f-1ubuntu2) ...

Processing triggers for libc-bin (2.39-0ubuntu8.6) ...

Q: Remove Implicit Dependency warning from Gradle output A:

Actually the correct fix for this warning, which became an error with Gradle 8, is to have a closer look into which files you copy to which directory.

The core problem is, that with your task writing directly to $buildDir Gradle can no longer detect which subdirectories you touch by doing so (because it doesnt keep track of that).

Your task copyConfiguration could completely overwrite the result of jacocoTestCoverageVerification depending on whether it is executed before or after. Therefore Gradle requires the user to define the order the tasks should be executed in.

That solution was described several times above, which is fine if there is no other way. Been there, done that.

But the best fix is actually to make sure you have dedicated directories for the task outputs you are generating. Change your copy-task spec to copy into an isolated subdirectory of the buildDir and the warning will go away because jacoco is not using any files in that specific directory:

val copyConfiguration by tasks.registering(Copy::class) {
    from("${projectDir}/configuration")
    into("${buildDir}/configuration")
}

If the resources should become part of a bigger artifact, consider retrieving them directly from the original location (your projectDir).

Q: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when trying to install tanstack A:

Looks like something is broken in the latest version (0.59.2) of the @tanstack/create-start script. 0.59.0 seems to be stable. Below is a snippet with npm:

npm create @tanstack/start@0.59.0

I have not used pnpm, but it would be in the lines of

pnpm create tanstack@0.59.0
